sources.author: Tennis Warehouse editorial team
sources.frame_or_tension: Editorial scores on page: control 93, power 42. Power basso per the page line 'With its firm construction, Confidential is not designed for the player who wants easy or "free" power'.
sources.quote: What isn't confidential is the nearly off-the-charts control score our team gave this string

sources.author: Michelle (TW playtester)
sources.frame_or_tension: Frame per WebFetch summary, not raw-verified: Wilson Pro Staff RF97 Autograph 58 lbs.
sources.quote: Confidential's stiff and low-powered response was perfect for my game

sources.author: Troy (TW playtester)
sources.frame_or_tension: Yonex EZONE 98+, settled on 47 lbs with a lock-out machine after adjusting. Power impression changed over time: 'My impressions on control and power changed somewhat over time'. Spin: 'Spin was great throughout the playtest, much like I find with Solinco Hyper-G'.
sources.quote: Initially, this string felt very control-oriented, somewhat dead and low powered

sources.author: TennisNerd reviewer (name not captured)
sources.frame_or_tension: Main review body. Also in body: 'Tension maintenance: After settling in after 1-2 hours, this string holds tension and playability extremely well.' and 'not for beginners or lower-level intermediate players'.
sources.quote: This string is all about control, so players who are just starting out would be better off with a softer string with a more powerful response.

sources.author: TennisNerd reader comment (name not captured)
sources.frame_or_tension: Reader comment on the same page, not the main review. Commenter was coming from Hyper G 16 at 52 lbs in a Prince Classic Graphite 100 at 52 lbs.
sources.quote: I find it more predictable than Hyper G, with similar characteristics in the spin and power department.

sources.author: Jon Crim
sources.frame_or_tension: Frame not stated. Scores on page per WebFetch: control 9.4, power 4.5, spin 9.1, comfort 6.1, durability 9.3.
sources.quote: Solinco Confidential excels in many areas, but one tradeoff that comes with its low power and control-centric performance is comfort.

sources.author: Lucasss
sources.frame_or_tension: Confidential 1.25 in Blade Pro Lab 98 16x19, strung 22/21 as written in the post. Based on the first hour only.
sources.quote: Gran pocketing, ottima potenza, tanto spin, non mi causato nessun dolore al braccio. Il controllo, seppur sia solo alla prima ora, è da riferimento.

sources.author: luigi.filippo
sources.frame_or_tension: Calibro 1.25. Tried on PA19 (as written) and Blade BLX 16/19. Feel and connection praised; no explicit control level given.
sources.quote: Pur essendo una corda orientata al controllo mi ha dato delle buone sensazioni in termini di feel e connessione con la racchetta.

sources.author: zomma1970
sources.frame_or_tension: Reply to a question asking whether to swap Hyper G 1.20 for Confidential in a T-Fight 305 XTC at 21/20. Comparison direction inferred from that question.
sources.quote: Sicuramente come prestazioni è più efficiente, anche se la comodità va un po' a donne di malaffare.

sources.author: nadavin95
sources.frame_or_tension: Frame not stated. Places Confidential between Hyper-G and Tour Bite Soft; no attribute named.
sources.quote: una via di mezzo tra le hyper g e le tour bite soft

models.summary: About 9 distinct people (Michelle and Troy both appear on one Tennis Warehouse page). Consensus is control alto and power basso, with spin high. Power perception varies: Troy says it firmed up and gained power over time, and one Italian poster (Lucasss, Blade 98 frame) says 'ottima potenza'. Comfort is the main complaint (TennisCompanion, zomma1970). Tension retention is praised (TennisNerd). Direct comparisons: spin similar to Hyper-G (TW Troy, TennisNerd reader), more predictable than Hyper-G (TennisNerd reader), placed between Hyper-G and Tour Bite Soft (nadavin95).

sources.author: Tennis Warehouse editorial team
sources.frame_or_tension: Editorial scores on page: control 9, spin 8. Page says 'it is still very much a control-oriented co-poly string'.
sources.quote: The original version of Confidential is very controlled and low powered, while Soft is slightly softer and provides a bit more power

sources.author: Michelle (TW playtester)
sources.frame_or_tension: Frame not captured. Michelle says the attribute was 'a little extra power', and the same page says 'Getting a little extra power without sacrificing control is a welcome attribute'.
sources.quote: I found a little more power than Solinco Hyper-G or standard Confidential, and thankfully, I didn't feel like I had to sacrifice control.

sources.author: Troy (TW playtester)
sources.frame_or_tension: Frame not captured. Found it 'a little more power than the standard version' but still with control.
sources.quote: this softer version of Confidential proved even more spin-friendly than the original

sources.author: Jon Crim
sources.frame_or_tension: Title: 'Arm-Friendly or Not?'. Scores per page: power 6.5, spin 8.8, control 8.9, comfort 7.9, durability 8.9. Notes 'a drop in spin and control' after roughly three to five hours.
sources.quote: Solinco Confidential Soft sits on the moderately powerful side for a polyester string.

sources.author: Chris Nash (per WebFetch summary, not raw-verified)
sources.frame_or_tension: Frames: Wilson Blade 98 and Babolat Pure Aero 98. Spec list: 'Power: Low to medium.' for Confidential Soft, 'Power: Medium.' for Hyper-G Soft. Tension holding is the main difference.
sources.quote: Choose Confidential Soft if you're looking for a softer, more regulated string with better tension holding.

models.summary: 5 entries; 4 distinct authors (Michelle and Troy share one Tennis Warehouse page). Consensus: slightly more power than standard Confidential (medio), more plush, still control-oriented. Versus Hyper-G Soft, Confidential Soft is the more controlled and better tension-holding option, while Hyper-G Soft has more spin and comfort. No Italian or TalkTennis source found for this model.

sources.author: Tennis Warehouse editorial team
sources.frame_or_tension: 16/1.30. Playtesters used 55 lbs in Prince Original Graphite 107 and Babolat Pure Drive Plus, and 48 lbs in Prince Extreme Warrior 107. Pros list 'Too firm and underpowered for beginners'.
sources.quote: Hyper-G was perfectly low-powered for our team; it enabled us to execute our most powerful strokes without having to worry about overhitting, but it never felt underpowered.

sources.author: Chris (TW playtester)
sources.frame_or_tension: Frame not captured. Same page as above.
sources.quote: Low on power, high on control -- this was my kind of string!

sources.author: Michelle (TW playtester)
sources.frame_or_tension: Tension range: she 'likes to test the upper limits of her racquet's tension range'. Hyper-G gave her no comfort issues in the high-50s range. Same person as the Confidential entries (counted once as a person).
sources.quote: I had no comfort issues at all during this playtest.

sources.author: Jon Crim
sources.frame_or_tension: Scores per page: control 9.5, power 4.7, spin 9.3, feel 8.9, comfort 6.8, durability 8.6. Arm note: 'its firmer feel can lead to discomfort over time'.
sources.quote: Hyper-G is unapologetically low-powered, and that’s part of its magic.

sources.author: Jon Levey
sources.frame_or_tension: Frame not stated. Spin: 'But overall, spin was a definite asset'. Feel: 'our testers didn't deem feel to be the Hyper-G's best attribute'.
sources.quote: Players using the strings are generally doing so for the heightened control and spin potential. Finding them to be underpowered is expected, and generally preferred.

sources.author: not captured
sources.frame_or_tension: Tested at 50 lbs and 55 lbs. Page also says 'the Solinco Hyper-G still offers a decent amount of power, especially when compared to similar strings'.
sources.quote: It’s no surprise that a control oriented string like the Solinco Hyper-G is also rather low-powered

models.summary: 6 entries from about 5 distinct people (Chris and Michelle are TW playtesters on one page). Consistent verdict: control alto, power basso, spin strong. Comfort is mixed: TennisCompanion rates it 6.8 and says it is firm, while TW's Michelle reported no comfort issues. Tension maintenance is praised in the TW review.

sources.author: Jon Crim
sources.frame_or_tension: Scores per page: power 6.0, spin 8.9, control 9.3, feel 8.6, comfort 8.0, durability 8.5. Comparisons per page: 'a moderate increase in power, especially compared to the original Hyper-G'; 'to be less stiff and more comfortable'.
sources.quote: Hand-in-hand with its lower power, Hyper-G Soft’s spin-friendly response plays a significant role in its excellent control.

sources.author: Chris Nash (per WebFetch summary, not raw-verified)
sources.frame_or_tension: Frames: Wilson Blade 98 and Babolat Pure Aero 98. Spec list: 'Spin: High.' Key trait: 'Easier access to spin and comfort than standard Hyper-G'.
sources.quote: If the primary things are spin and easier launch, I would choose Hyper-G Soft.

models.summary: Only 2 independent sources found (TennisCompanion and TennisNerd); not exhausted. Hyper-G Soft has more comfort and a bit more power than standard Hyper-G while keeping high control and spin. Versus Confidential Soft it has more spin and comfort and holds tension less well.

sources.quote: Low ish power, shaped, stiff ish (this one softer than the rest but still), spin friendly, colorful

sources.frame_or_tension: Agrees that there is 'power, but only compared to ultra-low powered polys'.
sources.quote: Yeah, there's power, but only compared to ultra-low powered polys like 4g and Confidential.

models.summary: 4 entries from TalkTennis (about 3 distinct posters plus one quoted). Mach-10 is described as the most powerful Solinco poly, but several posters call its power low-ish. Compared with Confidential it has more power.
